missed_issues: Skill files update themselves. On the first non-silent CLI run after a package upgrade, __main__.py:266-300 and 846-856 (`_refresh_stale_skills`) rewrite every user-scope SKILL.md that graphify installed, on all platforms (~/.claude/skills, ~/.codex/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ...). Only one .bak is kept (install.py ~376-381). skill.md:92 also runs an unpinned `uv tool install --upgrade`. Together this is a de facto auto-update channel for agent instructions. The only opt-out is GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1. It conflicts with OAW's 'nothing applies itself' rule and with pinned-SHA catalog evidence.

Data leaves the machine in skill mode without a prompt. skill.md:172-175: if GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY is set in the environment, the skill sends doc, PDF and image contents to Google's `gemini-3-flash-preview`, a preview model (llm.py:178-180). It prints only a tip and says 'do not wait for the user'. skill.md:170 also claims 'graphify does not read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY', but headless extract, label and prs auto-detect those keys (llm.py:3544-3548; prs.py:670-714).

The nested `claude -p` session runs with full agent context and no tool restrictions. llm.py:1911-1915 itself notes that the CLI layers in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills and MCP from cwd. cli_args (llm.py:1949-1953) pass no --allowedTools, --tools or --permission-mode. Untrusted corpus text is fed into an agentic session that inherits the user's permission allowlist and the project's hooks, including graphify's own PreToolUse guards. This opens a prompt-injection surface, risks recursion, and adds subscription spend. prs.py:709-714 runs a similar `claude -p` with PR metadata.

Code-derived data can leave the machine despite 'Code files: ... Nothing leaves your machine' (README.md:36, 432). `graphify cluster-only` and `graphify label` send community member labels (code identifiers) to an auto-detected API backend or to the claude -p fallback (llm.py:3790-3830, 3936-3949). The opt-outs are --no-label and GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none.

Git hooks and the merge driver are opt-in. They are installed only by an explicit `graphify hook install` (cli.py:1594-1603; references/hooks.md:10). Neither the skill nor `graphify install` adds them. The digest's 'what_it_does' implies they are part of the default agent-steering install.

`graphify claude install` writes a '## graphify' block into the project-root CLAUDE.md (install.py:2212-2229). `install --project` also writes .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills and .claude/settings.json (install.py:990-1003, 2051-2054). OAW's managed CLAUDE.md is supposed to only import AGENTS.md (oaw-ref/README.md:78), so this is a direct managed-file conflict, not just a possible one.

Windows-specific: the default install platform on Windows is 'windows' (install.py:2579). It installs skill-windows.md with a 50,457 B body, the largest variant. The hooks start graphify.exe on every Bash, Grep, Read and Glob call. The ~170 ms figure (install.py:500-502) is the project's own number, and Windows process startup has not been measured.

By default the Dockerfile serves MCP over HTTP on 0.0.0.0:8080 with no --api-key (Dockerfile CMD). serve.py:3373-3375 only prints a warning. If the 'other hosts via MCP' route is used, the graph is exposed without authentication.
callflow_html.py:1708 loads mermaid@11 from jsDelivr with a floating major version and no SRI integrity attribute. vis-network in exporters/html.py:733-735 is pinned and has SRI.

The video extra downloads faster-whisper model weights from Hugging Face on first use (transcribe.py:20, 150 `WhisperModel(model_name, ...)`). This network fetch is not mentioned in the privacy section. It downloads only and uploads no corpus data.
The Codex PreToolUse 'hook-check' entry has no timeout (install.py:1922-1931). It still starts a graphify process on every Codex Bash call even though it does nothing (cli.py:2971-2975).

BENCHMARKS.md describes a configuration this SHA does not ship ('hybrid retrieval', a dense RAG or hybrid RRF comparison, 'local embedder'; lines 11, 47-50, 183). The memory and crosstool harnesses are absent, so none of the published accuracy or cost figures can be attributed to this code.
integration_mode_note: I agree with absorb_method. Three things rule out a core or pack absorption: graphify needs non-stdlib native dependencies (pyproject.toml:14-54), every skill variant is over 48 KB, and it installs always-on routers and hooks. The OAW plan's own preference order puts 'absorb method' first (oaw-ref/docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md, section on digesting into nutrients). The source adds two reasons to be stricter about any later 'pack' route. First, `_refresh_stale_skills` rewrites installed SKILL.md copies automatically after upgrades, which breaks pinned-version evidence. Second, the Codex path OAW uses (.agents/skills) gets a variant whose subagent dispatch is wrong for Codex. Any pack must therefore force GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1, GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none (or an explicit --backend) and project-scope install without hooks, and must ship the codex variant at the OAW path. Two corrections to the digest's inputs: the reviewer-muzzling concern is narrower than stated, and git hooks are opt-in, not part of the default install. Neither changes the verdict.
